{{short description|French mathematician}}

[[File:Pierre Schapira ICM 2018 (30584816458).jpg|thumb|Pierre Schapira at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians|ICM]] 2018]]
'''Pierre Schapira''' (born April 28, 1943) is a French mathematician. He specializes in [[algebraic analysis]], especially [[Mikio Sato]]'s [[microlocal analysis]], together with the mathematical concepts of [[Sheaf (mathematics)|sheaves]] and [[derived categories]].

Schapira received his doctorate for work on [[hyperfunction]]s. Although these were already in use in France by [[André Martineau]], they were further developed by Schapira and [[Jacques-Louis Lions]]. This work earned Shapira an invitation to [[Kyoto University]], where he met [[Masaki Kashiwara]]. Together, they developed the microlocal theory of sheaves,<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Schapira |first1=Pierre |title=Sheaf Theory for Partial Differential Equations |journal=Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematics |date=29 August 1990 |volume=2 |issue=ICM-90 |page=1187 |url=https://www.mathunion.org/fileadmin/ICM/Proceedings/ICM1990.2/ICM1990.2.ocr.pdf |access-date=4 August 2022}}</ref> and have co-authored many papers spanning several decades.

He served as a professor at the [[Paris 13 University]] in the 1980s and has been a professor at the [[Pierre and Marie Curie University]] since the 1990s.

In 1990, he was an [[list of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers|invited speaker]] at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in [[Kyoto]], speaking on sheaf theory for [[partial differential equation]]s.<ref>{{cite web |title=Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematicians, Kyoto, Japan, 1990 |publisher=The Mathematical Society of Japan |url=https://www.mathunion.org/fileadmin/ICM/Proceedings/ICM1990.1/ICM1990.1.ocr.pdf |access-date=4 August 2022 }}</ref>

Schapira was inducted as a [[fellow]] of the [[American Mathematical Society]] with the Society's inaugural class of Fellows in 2013.<ref>{{cite web |title=2013 Class of Fellows of the AMS |url=http://www.ams.org/fellows_by_year.cgi?year=2013 |publisher=American Mathematical Society |access-date=4 August 2022 |archive-date=24 November 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221124200410/http://www.ams.org/fellows_by_year.cgi?year=2013 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
